organizations.normalization_notes: The contemporary 1933 source places Diettrich in the College of Commerce; the archival finding aid says College of Commerce and Journalism. Do not substitute Clark University, where he earned a degree, as an employer.

affiliations.date_precision: Appointment year 1931 documented by university finding aid; contemporary March 1933 magazine confirms instructor role. Wartime leave and exact OSS start date unknown.
affiliations.research_notes: University of Florida archives explicitly ties the distinctive full-name faculty member to OSS consultancy. The source does not prove an uninterrupted appointment immediately before consultancy or distinguish the timing of a Department of State assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Sigismond Diettrich has a high-confidence match to the University of Florida geographer Sigismond deRudesheim Diettrich.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon indexed name matches the university archival finding aid, which independently documents the same person's wartime OSS consultancy; a 1933 professional-society magazine confirms his Florida faculty appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from distinctive name plus a specific OSS association in an institutional archive; the Box 186 personnel file is not yet inspected.
claims.temporal_assessment: The archive places his university appointment in 1931 and OSS consultancy during World War II; exact service dates are missing.
claims.match_notes: The middle-name expansion is sourced from the university finding aid. No nationality or employer is inferred from education alone.

claims.claim_text: Sigismond Diettrich was employed by the University of Florida as an instructor of economic geography from 1931, before his wartime OSS consultancy.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The university's archival finding aid dates his faculty appointment to 1931 and separately records wartime OSS consultancy. A contemporary 1933 professional-society magazine identifies him as a University of Florida instructor of economic geography.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from distinctive indexed name and the finding aid's direct OSS linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; no source reviewed proves it was the immediately preceding affiliation or last civilian employer before OSS, because wartime leave and State Department timing remain unclear.
claims.match_notes: Publish as earlier documented employment, not an unqualified immediate predecessor. The institution was his employer, not merely an alma mater.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Reardon Dight has a high-confidence match to an official Army entry naming Reardon E Dight.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed and Army names share given and family names, while a nonshared protected identifier matches official Army bulk record ordinal 8637865.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the nonshared protected identifier; E is a sourced Army middle initial absent from the printed index.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army entry is wartime identity evidence only, not an OSS transfer date or named civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Do not expose the protected identifier or infer employer from occupation code.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Augustine M Digiovanni has a high-confidence wartime identity match to an official Army entry spelling the surname Di Giovanni.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A nonshared protected identifier agrees with official Army bulk record ordinal 3957574; the Army entry spaces the surname and omits the middle initial, while a Veterans Affairs memorial independently gives the indexed full name and Army service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from protected-identifier agreement, surname/given-name alignment, and independent official full-name corroboration.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official sources establish Army service but do not identify a pre-OSS employer or prove a 509th-to-OSS transfer sequence.
claims.match_notes: Preserve Digiovanni and Di Giovanni as source spellings. A privately reviewed 509th roster is only a unit lead, not a published transfer claim.
